_about: WHICH languages the model-free vocabulary corrector may run in, and HOW LOOSE it may be in
each. Transcribed from the shipping Windows table, src/Jot/Vocabulary/VocabularyLimits.cs in
jot-windows @ ae2ce1c, which is the source of truth for these numbers. There is no Swift
counterpart yet and NO TEST IN THIS PACKAGE READS THIS FILE — it is carried as data so a Swift
implementation has the measured values to build against instead of re-deriving them, and so
that a change to the shipped table can be diffed against something.

measurement.corpus: 9500 FLEURS clips of real speech through the shipping Nemotron engine and the real gate
budgetRule: Budget is 1.0 false applies per 1000 reference words, on a realistic 25-term list AND on a
mechanically adversarial one. A language at or above 0.9 (one measured event from the line)
gets the loosest distance that brings BOTH arms to <= 0.5. One that cannot reach that without
losing half its recall is not served at all. Nothing is tuned for a language the measurement

constants.noLimitMeaning: No cap beyond the corrector's own edit budget: one edit per five term characters, which tops out at a normalized distance of 0.33.
constants.unmeasuredMeaning: What an unmeasured language would get if one ever reached the corrector. Unreachable today, and deliberately the TIGHTEST shipped value rather than the loosest.

languages.note: Measured by E5, not E6: English runs the acoustic spotter, and this is the corrector's setting for the window before the 132 MB checkpoint arrives. Do not tighten without re-running E5.
Predicted to be the worst case on type coverage; the measurement says otherwise.
Long compounds, so 0.15 still allows an edit on most German words.
The frequency list covers 56.9 % of Greek running-text types, against 88.8 % of English — the brake is simply weaker here.

excluded.name: Slovenian
detail: The only setting that gets it under 0.5 is maxDistance 0.20, and at 0.20 it recovers 16 % of
missed terms — 43 % of what it recovers uncapped. A feature that corrupts at the budget line
and recovers one term in six is not a feature. The engine is also at 58.6 % WER in Slovenian,
so the premise (a mostly-right transcript with a few mis-spelled terms) does not hold.
This is an EXCLUSION WITH A REASON, not an omission: a frequency list ships, the language is
a supported engine locale, and it is still refused. Re-adding it needs a re-measurement, not

excluded.name: Serbian
detail: A 24 000-entry frequency list ships, so the brake WOULD work — but there is no Nemotron
locale for Serbian, so no setting can ever select it. Measured on Croatian audio as a probe;
enabling a language on a probe is not something to do.

excluded.name: Croatian
detail: No frequency list ships, so the common-word brake would be ABSENT, not merely weak — the
provider returns an empty set and the guard is inert. 'No brake ⇒ no run' is the rule that
keeps this off, and it is the same rule that keeps ar/ja/tr/mt off.

excluded.name: Arabic
detail: Same as Croatian: no frequency list, so no brake, so no run.

_alsoAbsent: ja, tr, mt and 'auto' are engine locales with no frequency list — same 'no brake ⇒ no run'
rule as hr/ar. They are listed here only so their absence is not read as an oversight.
